stories.headline: 2026 MLB division series Day 1: Live updates, lineups, analysis
stories.summary: All eight teams are in action Saturday, with three games down and one to go. Which clubs will come out strong?
stories.body:
It's Day 1 of the MLB division series!

The Chicago White Sox started the four-game Day 1 off by shutting out the Cleveland Guardians. Then, in the second game of the day Tarik Skubal helped the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 5-3 win over the Atlanta Braves. The Tampa Bay Rays downed the New York Yankees behind a dominant performance from ace Drew Rasmussen.

In the final game of the night, the San Diego Padres are taking on the No. 1 overall seed Milwaukee Brewers.

We've got you covered with pregame lineups, sights and sounds from the ballparks and postgame takeaways as each Day 1 matchup ends.

Key links: Mega-preview | Predictions | Bracket | Schedule

Jump to:

CHW-CLE | ATL-LAD | NYY-TB | SD-MIL

Sights and sounds
We have all the best moments from the ballparks as the division series begins.

Padres-Brewers

Follow live with pitch-by-pitch coverage

Chourio ties it up for the Brewers

Padres add to their early lead

Padres strike first in Milwaukee

Miz is bringing the heat

Takeaways

Tampa Bay Rays 1, New York Yankees 0
Tampa Bay leads series 1-0

It was over when ... Jonathan Aranda swatted a 2-2 changeup from Gerrit Cole over the right-field wall in the third inning. It was just a solo home run. The Yankees had six innings to match it. But they couldn't because Drew Rasmussen was that good. New York mustered just one hit and two walks against the right-hander over eight innings before Bryan Baker slammed the door on the win. Yankees batters piled up 12 strikeouts (10 against Rasmussen). That 18-run explosion in their wild-card round against the Red Sox suddenly seems like a distant memory.

Player who defined the game: Rasmussen's dominance of the Yankees -- he owned a 1.81 career ERA against them entering Saturday -- continued Saturday. He was on his way to delivering the fourth no-hitter in postseason history until Austin Wells cracked a line drive that landed on the chalk down the right-field line. But Wells then tried to stretch the easy double into a triple and was thrown out by several feet.

Otherwise, the Yankees had one baserunner reach second base -- Jazz Chisholm Jr. walked and stole second in the second inning. The Yankees barely touched Rasmussen and now face an 0-1 hole. -- Jorge Castillo

Key moments from Tampa Bay's win:

There goes the no-no -- but Wells gets thrown out on the bases

Rasmussen's no-hit bid now through seven innings

Drew Rasmussen has 10 strikeouts through seven no-hit innings and his pitch count is at 94.

Cole's night is done

Rasmussen is dealing for Rays

Aranda's blast gives Rays game's first lead

Boos are raining down already at the Trop

Los Angeles Dodgers 5, Atlanta Braves 3
Los Angeles leads series 1-0

It was over when ... Kyle Tucker got a fastball out over the plate and lifted it over the right-field wall. The Braves had cut their deficit to a single run in the prior half-inning, doing enough damage against Tarik Skubal to chase him out of the game. But then Tucker followed with a 408-foot two-run homer off AJ Smith-Shawver to make it a 4-1 game and give the Dodgers some cushion.

It was especially meaningful that Tucker provided it. His first year in L.A. was a disaster, especially at home, where he managed just two home runs through the month of August. But Tucker started to make some real progress with his swing in September. The Dodgers were hopeful that it would carry over into October. It seemingly has.

Player who defined the game: When the Dodgers dipped into their farm system to acquire Tarik Skubal ahead of the trade deadline, he was considered superfluous. As the next two months played out, with the offense struggling and Shohei Ohtani unavailable to pitch, Skubal began to look like a necessity. And after the smoke cleared on Game 1 of this NLDS, it became clear that he will be a lynchpin in the Dodgers' hopes of becoming the first NL team to three-peat as World Series champions.

Outside of a Sean Murphy home run, Skubal dominated the Braves despite pitching in 100-degree heat, consistently flirting with triple digits with his fastball and keeping hitters off balance with an excellent changeup. Before Murphy took him deep to begin the sixth inning, Skubal had retired 15 in a row, seven via strikeout.

What a Dodgers win means for Game 2: A lot about Sunday's Game 2 will be dictated by the Braves' pitching plans, particularly whether their ace, Chris Sale, is available for them. If Sale does start, it means he'd be lined up to start again on normal rest in a potential decisive Game 5. If he doesn't, it means the Braves will probably have to cobble together another bullpen game.

Manager Walt Weiss made it seem more likely that Sale would be pushed to Game 3 in Atlanta, given the four outs he recorded out of the bullpen in Game 3 of the wild-card round on Thursday night. But maybe the Braves losing Game 1, along with Sale doing some convincing, changes things.

Regardless, the Braves' offense will have to solve another two-time-Cy-Young Award-winning lefty in Blake Snell on Sunday. There's a reason the Dodgers are heavy favorites. -- Alden Gonzalez

Key moments from Los Angeles' win:

Braves cut deficit to 2 with blast from Albies in 9th -- but it's not enough

Tucker homers to give Dodgers 3-run lead

Murphy's home run pulls Braves within 1 run of L.A.

Dodgers get on board first with 2-run blast from Hernandez

Skubal answers with 3 K's of his own

Dodd strikes out the side for Atlanta

Chicago White Sox 3, Cleveland Guardians 0
Chicago leads series 1-0

It was over when ... Munetaka Murakami turned on a Parker Messick sinker and launched it 440 feet at 112.2 mph off the bat, a blast that put the White Sox up 2-0. The blow came minutes after Chicago's Bryan Hudson got Chase DeLauter on a fly ball to escape a base-loaded jam to end the third. There was a lot of game left at that point, but that sequence set the tone and the Guardians never really recovered.

Stat that defined the game: 6. That's the inning in which White Sox skipper Will Venable summoned Grant Taylor from the bullpen. Chicago led 2-0 at the time, and keep in mind, insofar as the White Sox have a closer, Taylor is the guy. But Venable has managed his team in playoff mode for weeks now, so of course Taylor laid four zeroes on Cleveland.

Per ESPN Research, his four-inning save is the third postseason save of four-plus innings pitched since 2000, joining Lance McCullers Jr. (2017) and Madison Bumgarner (2014 World Series) -- and it's the first four-inning save in Game 1 of a postseason series since saves became official in 1969.

It was a relief performance straight out of the 1970s. Goose Gossage and Sparky Lyle had to be proud.

What it means for the rest of the series: The White Sox showed how tough their pitching staff can be when playing from ahead. As mentioned, they have been in this mode for a lot of games by now, putting all their available resources into winning the game in front of them. Then they figure out the next game when it arrives. Cleveland needs to jump on the White Sox early so the Guardians, not Venable, can dictate how the game will be played. -- Bradford Doolittle

Key moments from Chicago's win:

Guardians turn potential 3-run homer into inning-ending double play

Murakami blasts 2-run home run to give White Sox the lead

stories.headline: Lightning beat the Capitals 3-1 in home opener
stories.summary: — Andrei Vasilevskiy made 19 saves, Charle-Edouard D'Astous and Conor Geekie scored in the first period and the Tampa Bay Lightning won their home opener with a 3-1 victory over the Washington Capitals on Saturday night.
stories.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — Andrei Vasilevskiy made 19 saves, Charle-Edouard D'Astous and Conor Geekie scored in the first period and the Tampa Bay Lightning won their home opener with a 3-1 victory over the Washington Capitals on Saturday night.


Brandon Hagel had two assists for the Lightning, and Jake Guentzel scored into an empty net and had an assist. Tampa Bay opened play Thursday night in New York with a 5-1 loss to the Rangers.


Charlie Lindgren finished with 27 saves for Washington. Justin Sourdif scored for the Capitals.


D'Astous put Tampa Bay up 1-0 at 2:26 of the opening period as he cut down from the point into the middle slot to take a pass from Brandon Hagel and zipped a wrist shot past Lindgren.


The Lightning finished off the period with a goal from Geekie, who was off the right wing side to take a pass from Hagel for a quick shot to the inside of the post with 3:30 top go for a 2-0 lead.


The Capitals, who opened Friday with a win in Carolina, cut the deficit in half in the second period on a redirect from Sourdif off a point shot from Jacob Chychurn.


Guentzel scored with 2:05 left in the third.


Washington played the third period without defenseman Matt Roy, who suffered a lower-body injury and did not return.


Tampa Bay defenseman John Carlson, who spent 17 seasons with the Capitals, played his first career game against Washington, picking up an assist on the empty-net goal.


Up next
Capitals: Host Pittsburgh on Wednesday night.


Lightning: Host Philadelphia on Monday night.

stories.headline: UFC 332: Live results, analysis for Silva vs. Wang
stories.summary: Natalia Silva and Wang Cong clash for the vacant women's flyweight title at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City.
stories.body:
The UFC will crown a new women's flyweight champion Saturday, when 29-year-old Natalia Silva and Wang Cong, 34, square off in the main event of UFC 332 at Delta Center in Salt Lake City. Former champion Valentina Shevchenko vacated the belt because of an undisclosed injury in September.

Silva, ESPN's No. 2-ranked flyweight contender and No. 9 on ESPN's MMA 30 under 30 list, is undefeated inside the Octagon. She has won eight consecutive fights. Silva's most recent win was a unanimous decision over former two-time strawweight champion Rose Namajunas.

Wang enters on a four-fight winning streak, during which each victory has come by unanimous decision. Most recently, Wang beat Tracy Cortez at UFC 329 in July.

In the co-main event, rising men's bantamweight challenger Payton Talbott faces his biggest test yet against former two-time men's flyweight titleholder Deiveson Figueiredo.

Brett Okamoto, Jeff Wagenheim and Dre Waters break down all the action from UFC 332.

stories.headline: Lakers' Ziaire Williams proposes to longtime girlfriend at Bruno Mars tour
stories.summary: The singer complemented the proposal during his second of five Inglewood shows.
stories.body:
Pop superstar Bruno Mars knows how to put on a good show. But on Friday night, one audience member seemed to steal the show from the 16-time Grammy winner.

As Mars performed "Marry You" during his second night of five in Inglewood, California, for "The Romantic Tour," Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams found the perfect moment to make a promise for forever.

On the floor level of SoFi Stadium, Williams got down on bended knee as Mars sang the words "I think I wanna marry you," lining up his question -- "Will you marry me?" -- with the lyrics.

As Williams proposed to his teary-eyed girlfriend, model Paris Timan, Mars blended his singing with his excitement, crooning, "Please say I do I do I do."

After Timan -- who seemed to be in shock -- said yes, Mars continued singing through the song's conclusion while the couple shared a hug as the audience erupted in cheers.

Timan will be part of two new beginnings for Williams. In July, the 25-year-old signed a one-year, $3 million deal with the Lakers after a 2025-26 season in which he posted 10.2 points and 2.4 rebounds per game in 54 games with the Brooklyn Nets.

And the next part? Planning the rest of their lives together. Nothing screams "fairy tale" more than a proposal to a Mars love song.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu (Manchester United)

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Denmark head coach Brian Riemer told broadcaster TV2 after the game: "He has an injury and has to go home."

Cody Gakpo (Liverpool)

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

Noussair Mazraoui (Manchester United)

The United full-back was forced out of Morocco's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Lesotho after 69 minutes. He was holding his back while on the floor after a challenge.

Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City)

O'Reilly missed England's win against Czechia on Tuesday night after also missing training on Monday. Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha was called into the matchday squad. O'Reilly returned to Manchester for further treatment before England played Croatia.

Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham Hotspur)

The Tottenham defender Jan Paul van Hecke picked up a foot injury in the Netherlands' clash with Serbia and withdrew from the Netherlands' squad during a training session.

No replacement will be called up for van Hecke. He is now returning to Spurs.

Christos Tzolis (Arsenal)

The Greece winger limped out of his side's draw against the Netherlands after just 18 minutes.

Tzolis pulled his shirt over his head and looked upset as he left the match early.

He represents another headache for Arsenal after Kai Havertz's prior injury for Germany.

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

stories.headline: 'Thought I was going to die': crash rocks Knights fans
stories.summary: Chris Clancy was one of thousands of Newcastle Knights fans who lined the streets to farewell his team as they travelled to Sydney for the grand final.
stories.body:
Chris Clancy was one of thousands of Newcastle Knights fans who lined the streets to farewell his team as they travelled to Sydney for the grand final.

But he was left injured, along with nine other people, when a car driven by an 18-year-old P-plater careered into a crowd gathered on the side of the road near a major roundabout.

Mr Clancy was with his nephews waiting to cheer the Knights when disaster struck on Saturday.

"We're there at the roundabout having fun -- cars going past, beeping their horns, people waving," he told AAP.

"The next thing, this car stops (at) the roundabout and then he just floored it on the wet ground, lost it.

"It happened in seconds, but when you stand there, seeing the car coming at you, I honestly thought I was going to die. It just felt like slow motion."

Mr Clancy suffered small fractures in his ribs and spine and a broken collarbone.

In addition, his foot was injured after the car ran over it while the motorist was allegedly trying to drive away.

"I dragged myself across the ground because I couldn't stand at the time, trying to get my foot out, which luckily I did," Mr Clancy said.

The driver was taken to hospital for mandatory testing and subsequently charged with nine offences, including dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm, negligent driving and causing bodily harm by misconduct.

He was refused bail and is due to appear in court on Sunday.

Police said two other people in the car were escorted from the crash scene after the crowd turned on them.

Investigators did not believe the incident was deliberate but declined to comment on reports the vehicle was being driven erratically before the crash.

At least seven people remain at John Hunter Hospital with injuries caused by the collision.

They include a five-year-old girl who was placed into an induced coma with critical injuries, although her condition has stabilised.

A 67-year-old man was also hospitalised in a serious but stable condition.

Mr Clancy expressed gratitude to those who provided help after the accident, including a woman who stayed with him and his nephews and took his car home for him, and a man who pushed his nephew Thomas out of harm's way.

Several Knights players sent him their well-wishes via social media, including club captain Kalyn Ponga.

"All the best with the recovery mate! The team and community are with yas (sic)," he wrote.

Knights chief executive Peter Parr expressed deep concern for those impacted by the crash.

"Newcastle is a strong community," he said.

"We have seen that strength throughout this week and today we need to draw on it again with compassion, care and support for those who need it most," he said.

A diehard Knights supporter who has had season tickets for several years, Mr Clancy told doctors they could operate on his collarbone as long as it didn't clash with his team's grand final face-off with the Sydney Roosters on Sunday night.

"Either way, the guys have done our town proud," he said.

stories.headline: MMA 30 under 30: Champions Joshua Van and Usman Nurmagomedov lead
stories.summary: The future is now! Joshua Van, Usman Nurmagomedov and more championship-caliber fighters top 30 under 30 list.
stories.body:
ESPN's yearly list of the top 30 fighters under age 30 can be characterized as a look into the future. These are the young fighters who presumably will take over once the sport's top veterans move on.

But this year's ranking is not merely forward thinking.

Consider that the top two fighters -- Joshua Van in the UFC and Usman Nurmagomedov in the PFL -- aren't rising prospects. They are defending champions. No. 3 Ilia Topuria is a former UFC champion. And Natalia Silva, who sits at No. 9, will go for the vacant women's flyweight title this weekend at UFC 332. In MMA, it seems, "the future is now" is not simply a catchy slogan.

There also are up-and-comers in these rankings, as there are every year, and many who have appeared before are now in different positions, as a year's worth of fight results dictates.

Our panel -- Brett Okamoto, Dre Waters, Jeff Wagenheim, Andrew Davis, James Regan, Sam Bruce, James Dielhenn, Marcus Vanderberg and Alecia Hamm -- selected fighters based on their achievements this year and their potential. Okamoto, Waters and Wagenheim provide breakdowns of the top 30 under 30.

1. Joshua Van

UFC men's flyweight champion

Age: 24

2025 rank: 3

It takes a remarkable athlete to lead this type of list -- but to lead it at 24 years old is just absurd. Van is arguably the purest talent the sport has seen in years. No one could have predicted at the start of 2025, when his ascension truly took off, that he would end the year as ESPN's best breakout fighter. He is undeniably the best active flyweight on the planet and has the personality and charisma to match. Sean O'Malley recently proclaimed on his YouTube channel that Van will go down as the "greatest flyweight of all time." After Van's second win over former longtime champion Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 331, who wants to disagree? -- Okamoto

2. Usman Nurmagomedov

PFL lightweight champion

Age: 28

2025 rank: 7

It's unusual for a fighter outside the UFC to establish himself as the best in his weight class, but that's exactly what Nurmagomedov has done with his perfect 21-0 record. It's not unreasonable to suggest Nurmagomedov would be favored against any other 155-pound fighter in the world, including top-ranked UFC lightweights Justin Gaethje, Arman Tsarukyan and Ilia Topuria. Nurmagomedov is currently a free agent, and his next move is one of the biggest questions in MMA this year. -- Okamoto

3. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 1

Topuria entered the year as the UFC lightweight champion, ESPN's top-ranked fighter under 30 and on the short list of the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world. He got his first chance to defend the belt in a main event at the White House on June 14, but the challenger, Gaethje, handed him the first loss of his professional career, retiring him on the stool after four rounds. Despite the loss, Topuria remains one of MMA's best young fighters. -- Waters

4. Michael Morales

UFC welterweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: 5

Fans love a good knockout, and Morales has handed out KOs regularly on his way to the welterweight title picture. Three consecutive first-round finishes have all the momentum on Morales's side, but he hasn't fought yet this year. He's on champion Islam Makhachev's radar as a future welterweight challenger, but he'll likely need one more win against a top contender to get his first title shot. -- Okamoto

5. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL women's flyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 2

One of the most destructive figures in women's MMA, Ditcheva is uniquely violent, boasting a 73% knockout rate in the PFL. The question isn't whether she can be a star, it's how big her star can become. With Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions acquiring the PFL going into 2027, we will find out what the ceiling is for Ditcheva's exposure. She is exactly the kind of marketable athlete MVP will get behind. -- Okamoto

6. Song Yadong

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 28

Song put two years of little activity behind him by fighting three times in the first eight months of 2026. He lost a tight decision to Sean O'Malley in January, but he bounced back in May against another champion, choking out Deiveson Figueiredo. But what elevated Song most on this list -- he was way down at No. 28 last year -- was his knockout of Umar Nurmagomedov in August. That stunning result boosted Song's stock as a men's bantamweight contender. Next up should be another ranked opponent, giving him an opportunity to build off of his recent success. -- Wagenheim

7. Josh Hokit

UFC heavyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Hokit's antics on the microphone may not have endeared him to UFC CEO Dana White, who said at UFC 331 that he doesn't like anything Hokit says. But the heavyweight's performance in his second year in the Octagon has skyrocketed him to the top of the division. "I say it all the time: I don't have to like you for you to thrive here and you to do well and be successful," White said of Hokit's ascension. With just four UFC fights under his belt -- three this year -- Hokit is set to challenge Ciryl Gane for the heavyweight championship in the main event at UFC 334 in November. Hokit, who earned a contract on Season 9 of "Dana White's Contender Series" just 13 months ago, already has beaten heavyweight stalwarts Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis in two of the more entertaining fights of the year. Ending 2026 with a UFC championship would be an impressive cap to his year. -- Waters

8. Ian Machado Garry

UFC welterweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 6

Love him or hate him, Machado Garry might be the best UFC welterweight not named Islam Makhachev. He took the pound-for-pound king five competitive rounds in August and is still in great position to accept some of the biggest fights available as he works his way back toward a second title shot. Machado Garry has said he believes that a loss to Makhachev will only make him better, and there are plenty of reasons to believe the 28-year-old's best is still in front of him. -- Okamoto

9. Natalia Silva

UFC women's flyweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 9

Silva might be a UFC champion by the end of the weekend. By winning 14 fights in a row, the past eight in the Octagon, she has been looking more and more like championship material. Her three most recent wins came against former titleholders Jessica Andrade, Alexa Grasso and Rose Namajunas. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva is poised to take over if she handles Wang Cong at UFC 332. Women's flyweight is a highly competitive division, with several pound-for-pound elites. It could be Silva's domain until someone figures out how to contend with her slick movement. -- Wagenheim

10. Quillan Salkilld

UFC lightweight

Age: 26

2025 rank: 23

Somehow, even in a division full of potential superstars, Australia's Salkilld has managed to stand out -- and not just because he has a great mustache. Salkilld's got a look and presence on social media that plays well with the UFC's fanbase, and he has substance to back up the flash. He is on a streak of five consecutive first-round finishes, including in his most recent win, in which he beat submission artist Mateusz Gamrot at his own game with a first-round rear-naked choke. Salkilld has that "it" factor, and if he keeps winning, he will collide with some of the sport's biggest names. -- Okamoto

11. Jean Silva

UFC featherweight

Age: 29

Last year's rank: 15

Silva was denied a higher-profile opportunity when his Noche UFC opponent, popular and flashy Yair Rodriguez, withdrew from last month's fight because of injury. Silva did not suffer a letdown against late replacement Jose Miguel Delgado, taking care of business by doing what he usually does: making the fight his showcase. The win was Silva's second in a row after a September 2025 knockout loss ended a 13-fight winning streak. Silva is building himself toward featherweight contention with an aggressive fighting style that is a dream for fans and a nightmare for opponents. -- Wagenheim

12. Tatsuro Taira

UFC men's flyweight

Age: 26

Last year's rank: 22

Taira won eight of his first nine UFC fights, a run of success capped by a knockout of former two-time men's flyweight champion Brandon Moreno in December. But it was a loss that drew more attention to him -- positive attention. Taira ended up being knocked out by current champion Joshua Van in a title fight in May, but it was a back-and-forth fight that lasted into the fifth round. Taira put the champ in trouble with eight takedowns and over 10 minutes of control time. It was fight of the night, keeping the Japanese fighter in the contender conversation. -- Wagenheim

13. Navajo Stirling

UFC light heavyweight

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

Entering 2026, all three of Stirling's UFC wins had come by unanimous decision, but that stretch seems like an anomaly now. Stirling earned a UFC contract via a second-round knockout on "Dana White's Contender Series" in 2024 and had knocked out three of his four professional opponents before that. He officially refound his finishing ways this year, winning each of his three fights by knockout, including a first-round TKO over former light heavyweight champion Jan Blachowicz in August. Stirling may not have opened the year nearing his first title shot, but if he can take down another former champion in JiYí Procházka on Nov. 21, he'll end the year near the top of the light heavyweight contenders short list. -- Waters

14. Thad Jean

PFL welterweight champion

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

The PFL has asked several figures to be the "face of the company" over the years with mixed results. Recently much of that promotional expectation has been heaped on Jean, the 28-year-old who won the 2025 welterweight tournament. Jean has legitimate skills and highlight-reel potential. He's styled on the opponents he should have, and has proven his world-class merit with hard-fought wins over tougher opponents such as Logan Storley and Jason Jackson. -- Okamoto

15. Gabriel Bonfim

UFC welterweight

Age: 29

Last year's rank: 21

Bonfim is another fighter on this list who could be nearing a title shot. He only has competed once this year, but was dominant in a five-round unanimous decision win over former welterweight champion Belal Muhammad. All three judges scored the fight 50-45 for Bonfirm, who claimed the No. 7 spot in ESPN's divisional rankings as a result. Bonfim's biggest hurdle going forward will be the rise in competition in a stacked 170-pound division. His next test will come against No. 6-ranked Sean Brady on Nov. 7. -- Waters

16. Salahdine Parnasse

UFC lightweight

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

It's been an interesting year for Parnasse. In January, he defended his lightweight championship in the Polish fight promotion KSW, winning by knockout. He vacated that title to fight on the first MMA card for Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions brand. Parnasse scored a first-round knockout over Kenneth Cross on the undercard of the most-watched MMA event ever. Last month he made his UFC debut, scoring another knockout -- his sixth in a row. The first-round finish of Dan Hooker doesn't make Parnasse a contender, but he's someone to keep watching. -- Wagenheim

17. Ateba Gautier

UFC middleweight

Age: 24

Last year's rank: NR

Gautier is an absolute wrecking ball of a human. Nine of his 11 career wins have come by knockout, including seven in the first round. Potential? Off the charts. Momentum? Undeniable. The only question around Gautier isn't about him, but his opposition. His five UFC opponents have a 4-14 combined record inside the Octagon. That will change when he meets Roman Kopylov (15-5) this weekend at UFC 332. If Gautier knocks out Kopylov, his hype will be validated. -- Okamoto

18. Erin Blanchfield

UFC women's flyweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: 11

Blanchfield has been included on ESPN's list of top young prospects nearly every year since she signed with the UFC in 2021. She was ESPN's No. 1 prospect under 25 in 2023, but missed the cut the following year after suffering a one-sided drubbing to Manon Fiorot. She bounced back from that loss with back-to-back wins over Rose Namajunas and Tracy Cortez and is scheduled to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius on Oct. 17 in a battle of top-10 flyweights. -- Waters

19. Payton Talbott

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 20

You know a young fighter is someone the UFC considers a rising prospect when you start to see him booked against championship-decorated opponents. Talbott is coming off a December win that was convincing enough to send former two-division titlist Henry Cejudo into retirement. This weekend at UFC 332, Talbott will take on another former belt-holder, Deiveson Figueiredo. These kinds of fights draw attention, even when they're against faded stars. If Talbott is successful again, he could be on his way toward ranked opposition and a slow, steady build. -- Wagenheim

20. Lone'er Kavanagh

UFC men's flyweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: NR

He can't live on one performance forever, but Kavanagh's five-round victory over former champion Brandon Moreno in February -- in Mexico, on short notice -- said a lot about this 27-year-old's capabilities. He's 1-2 in his past three appearances, but Kavanagh has a tantalizing amount of potential. How big would a Joshua Van vs. Lone'er Kavanagh title fight be, if Kavanagh were to get on a roll and give England a shot at its next UFC champion? -- Okamoto

21. Paul Hughes

PFL lightweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 16

Hughes came up short in two attempts to take the PFL lightweight championship from Nurmagomedov last year. Despite losing both fights by decision, Hughes proved himself to be one of the best lightweights in the world. He has been out of action this year due to a knee injury, but now that Nurmagomedov is a free agent, there's a chance for Hughes to challenge for the PFL title again immediately upon returning to active status. -- Waters

22. Gable Steveson

UFC heavyweight

Age: 26

2025 rank: NR

Steveson was about 12 seconds from being a whole lot higher on this list. As an Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was as highly anticipated a prospect as the sport has seen when he transitioned to MMA last year. After winning his first four pro fights by first-round knockout, including his UFC debut in July, Steveson looked like a heavyweight with which to be reckoned. He still might turn into that guy, but getting KO'd by the second punch heavy underdog Sean Sharaf threw at him at UFC 331 two weeks ago put the brakes on the Steveson hype train. The big dude has work to do. -- Wagenheim

23. Muhammad Mokaev

Brave CF men's flyweight champion

Age: 26

2025 rank: 27

One of the most unique -- and frustrating -- careers in MMA continues to play out outside the UFC. It's now been 26 months since Mokaev parted ways with the promotion. It's worth noting that Mokaev's last fight in the UFC was a victory over Manel Kape, who is widely expected to be the next title challenger for Van. Will we ever see a day when Mokaev can return? At the moment, there doesn't seem to be much of a thaw from the UFC side. But Mokaev is still 26 years old and still unbeaten. He's so young and freakishly good that it's impossible to count out any opportunity forever. -- Okamoto

24. Valter Walker

UFC heavyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Walker has been the epitome of a one-trick fighter so far in his UFC career. But if his one trick isn't broken, why fix it? Since losing by unanimous decision in his UFC debut in 2024, Walker has been on an absolute tear, beating each of his past five opponents by first-round submission. Four of those finishes have come via heel hook. It wasn't until his most recent victory over Thomas Petersen that the submission ace had to show more of his ability, transitioning from his signature heel hook attempt into a calf slicer submission for the finish. -- Waters

25. David Martinez

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Look no further than the UFC's matchmaking to decipher how promising Martinez is. The UFC tried to pair him with Umar Nurmagomedov in July, but Martinez was forced to withdraw because of injury. He has quietly taken out some of the most respected veterans in the bantamweight division -- Dan Ige, Marlon Vera and Rob Font -- over the past 12 months and is on the cusp of a top-five ranking. Martinez lacks some of the star power of other names on this list, but he's likely to draw big-name opponents in the near future. Consistent results would inevitably skyrocket every aspect of his career. -- Okamoto

26. Tommy McMillen

UFC featherweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

McMillen, who trains with former UFC men's bantamweight champion Sean O'Malley, has had a breakout performance this year. He earned a UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series" a year ago and has strung together three straight wins since. He was tested in his most recent bout, a unanimous decision win over Marwan Rahiki, but he outpointed Rahiki on all three of the judges' scorecards. He's earned the right to take a step up in competition in his next Octagon appearance. -- Waters

27. Jose Miguel Delgado
UFC featherweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Delgado was victorious in four of his first five trips to the Octagon before running into Jean Silva in the main event of Noche UFC last month. Fighting on short notice, Delgado lost by third-round submission, but he won the first round and held his own until running low on energy, whereupon Silva took over. His success in the early rounds gives Delgado building blocks for the future. -- Wagenheim

28. Raul Rosas Jr.

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 21

2025 rank: 30

Still just 21 years old, Rosas is 7-1 in the UFC -- and the context around some of those wins is starting to grow. No longer is Rosas a phenom teenager operating on UFC prelims. Coming off his first UFC main event on Sept. 26, Rosas now holds two significant wins over proven veterans in Rob Font and Raoni Barcelos and is a ranked UFC bantamweight ... all before his 22nd birthday next week. There is no comparison to Rosas when it comes to experience gained at such a young age. There are plenty of steps between where he is now and a UFC championship, but he's certainly on the right path. -- Okamoto

29. Baisangur Susurkaev

UFC middleweight

Age: 25

2025 rank: 25

Susurkaev, a longtime training partner of former champion Khamzat Chimaev, made a name for himself last summer when he earned a UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series" then made his official debut four days later at UFC 319. He finished both of his opponents in those contests. In his lone appearance this year, Susurkaev picked up another finish, beating Djorden Santos by third-round submission in May. Next, he'll take on a fellow unbeaten prospect Donte Johnson at UFC 334 in November. A win over Johnson could establish Susurkaev as a future problem for top middleweight fighters. -- Waters

30. Iasmin Lucindo

UFC strawweight

Age: 24

2025 rank: 29

Lucindo had won five of six fights and was on the rise before an injury and a failed drug test in September 2025 derailed her. She withdrew from a fight with strawweight contender Gillian Robertson and ended up being suspended for a year, while Robertson went on to a title challenge. Lucindo is eligible to compete again, and at 24 years old she has time to build herself back up to contendership in the 115-pound division. -- Wagenheim

stories.headline: LeBron James calls scrimmage 'great first step' for new-look 76ers
stories.summary: Throngs of fans waited in lines more than 10-deep to watch LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and the rest of the 76ers take part in Saturday's scrimmage.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- It might have been the basketball equivalent of a dress rehearsal, but the 76ers' intrasquad scrimmage Saturday certainly gave a promising glimpse of what could be in store when the curtain actually comes up for the 2026-27 NBA season.

Philadelphia hosted its annual Blue-White game in front of approximately 10,000 fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena, moving the exhibition from their G League affiliate's home in Delaware to accommodate the added interest in the new-look team.

While throngs of fans waited in lines more than 10-deep in the atrium an hour before the noon start, there was plenty of on-court action from LeBron James, Jaylen Brown & Co. to enjoy as soon as the scrimmage started.

"To be able to take what we've done on the practice floor, bring it to a game floor situation around our fans ... it was a great first step in the direction we're trying to go," James said.

Longtime Sixers public address announcer Matt Cord, who had retired before deciding to come back once Philadelphia had its historic summer, announced the starters for the Blue team.

First Tyrese Maxey, then VJ Edgecombe, then Brown, then James and then the man in the middle who has been with the franchise for 13 years.

"7-2 from Cameroon, No. 21, Joel 'The Processsss' Embiiddddd!" Cord bellowed.

"It doesn't matter who gets announced first, last, second, third," Embiid said.

But the cheers that followed every name did mean something to him.

"We love the fans," Embiid said. "We want them, and we need them to be part of this. I mentioned it at media day: It's already hard enough to win as a group that gets together for the first year. So we're going to need all we can, whether it's from everybody in this building, the fans, the outside people, we're going to need to get together. We're going to need all the support possible."

The Sixers didn't keep an official box score, but the stats mattered far less than some of the sequences that showed the early chemistry that is developing after a week of training camp, including James finding a trailing Embiid for an above-the-break 3.

"Guys are going to use their speed against people and try to score a quick basket, and if we don't have anything, I'm the trail guy," Embiid said matter-of-factly.

Both Maxey and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope delivered feeds to James for alley-oop dunks that the 41-year-old star finished with ease. Embiid got his 7-foot frame to lift high enough to both block springy second-year guard Edgecombe and have a dunk of his own.

"Pretty good, not bad," a noticeably slimmed-down Embiid said when asked how he felt physically compared to last season. Then he showed his sense of humor is as strong as ever.

"That's probably the last dunk of my career," Embiid said with a smirk.

While James has had only four official Sixers practices, plus the scrimmage, it was enough for him to conclude that Embiid is a different player than the guy he won a gold medal with at the Paris Olympics two summers ago.

"The difference between '24 and now, he's just so much more healthier," James said. "He hasn't missed a practice. He's been in damn near everything that we've done. Pretty much. They've had to sit him out at times, even when he wanted to keep going. ... So it's been good. Actually, great."

Philadelphia limited the scrimmage to three 10-minute quarters but started each period with the scoreboard set to 80-80 to simulate an end-of-game scenario.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse, who thanked the crowd for its support after the scrimmage, is giving the team the day off Sunday before it opens its four-game preseason slate by hosting the New York Knicks on Monday.

"It will be good to get out there with some of our guys to just get a rhythm," James said of the preseason schedule. "At the same time, also not overdo it, because we're putting a lot into our practices right now, fine-tuning what we want to do once the [regular-season] games come, but there'll be opportunities when we get out there in the preseason."

stories.headline: Fever's Mitchell says she'll be 'selfish' with free agency call
stories.summary: Retaining unrestricted free agent Kelsey Mitchell is a top offseason priority for the Fever, according to general manager Amber Cox and coach Stephanie White.
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Retaining unrestricted free agent Kelsey Mitchell is a top offseason priority for the Indiana Fever, both general manager Amber Cox and coach Stephanie White acknowledged Saturday morning. The four-time All-Star had a career year in which she set the WNBA single-season records for points scored and 3-point field goals made.

Mitchell, however, said she will be "selfish" with her decision-making.

"I have to be selfish," Mitchell said during her end-of-season media session. "I think that's where I am in my career ... what I probably need and what's probably best for me. So I have to be selfish in that room.

"But I think, ultimately, being on the Fever and being a part of an organization that does come with a lot of ups and downs, what factors in and what is important for me is, obviously, having a good chemistry on and off the floor. I've only been with one team my entire career, so it's all kind of like figuring this out. It's hard, man."

Mitchell ranked No. 2 in the league with a career-high 24.7 points per game while shooting 50.9% from the field and 45.0% from behind the arc. She is expected to receive a high number of MVP votes and be named all-WNBA first team for the second season in a row.

Cox said the goal is to have Mitchell retire in a Fever uniform.

"She has a lot of equity in this franchise and has put in a lot of time," Cox said. "She's meant so much to us and has, obviously, had, arguably, the best season in the history of our league in terms of being a scoring guard. The numbers she put up were just spectacular, and you hear night in and night out from players across this league -- the hardest person to guard in this league is Kelsey Mitchell.

"When you put her in the backcourt with Caitlin [Clark] ... historic in terms of what they were able to do, and we hope we have the opportunity to build upon that."

Mitchell and Clark became the highest-scoring duo in WNBA history as they led highest-scoring offense in league history. The 30-year-old Mitchell also set the league record for the most consecutive games scoring 20-plus points (27). She received the core designation from the team the past two seasons and cannot receive it again.

Being in a backcourt with Clark is something Mitchell values, she explained, and that will be important in her decision-making. But Mitchell added that playing in Indiana and with Clark can be difficult due to the vitriol from some fans.

"It's a lot to hash out," Mitchell said. "I just think that I've got to be selfish about where my career is going a little bit in terms of some of the things, as I get older, what's important for me, whether it be winning, whether it be my own individual success. I worked my tail off to be here, though, man. So whatever I do, it's gonna come from a selfish standpoint. I'll be honest about that."

A more difficult decision for the Fever lies with unrestricted free agent Sophie Cunningham. The eight-year veteran had a strong start to the season and was even considered a Sixth Player of the Year candidate after the first two months, but she cooled down the stretch. She finished with 7.9 points per game, her lowest scoring average since 2023.

Controversy also swirled around Cunningham on multiple occasions for her comments to ESPN regarding transgender athletes, a kerfuffle with DiJonai Carrington and a finger-pointing incident with DeWanna Bonner. Cunningham is outspoken on social media and her podcast. Protesters and supporters began to show up outside arenas after Cunningham's comments regarding transgender athletes in women's sports.

Cox said non-basketball-related situations would not influence her evaluation of Cunningham.

"Sophie's had two really productive years for us in terms of shooting the basketball," Cox said. "She is a really solid leader in the locker room, a great connector. She brings levity but also brings a lot of experience. She's serious and is an important voice in our locker room when we need it. When we really need to lock in.

"She's an unrestricted free agent, so we look forward to having those conversations. Again, she had a really productive year, and we'll see just where things take us."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Haaland wants LaLiga move over Arsenal
stories.summary: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland favors a move to Spain over Arsenal. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester City striker Erling Haaland favors a move to Spain over Arsenal, while Barcelona retain interest in Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester City striker Erling Haaland favors a move to Spain over Arsenal, despite the Gunners having the financial muscle to pursue him, reports TEAMtalk. After news of City's financial charges that could result in the club's relegation, Haaland's camp has identified 2027 as a potential departure date from the Etihad for the Norway striker, though his contract runs to 2034. And Barcelona will be looking to put themselves in pole position for his signature alongside Real Madrid if he becomes available.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi is keen on a reunion with the 29-year-old Japan international, who played under him at Brighton, but Mitoma is also attracting interest from Liverpool as his contract approaches its final 18 months.

The Bianconeri have kept an eye on their former youth player for several seasons when he moved to Gozzano and Fiorentina, before starring at Brentford, while Fiorentina midfielder Cher Ndour and Borussia Dortmund youngster Samuele Inácio are also under consideration.

- Liverpool winger Federico Chiesa is open to a return to Serie A ahead of the January transfer window, according to Calciomercato. Internazionale, Atalanta and Lazio are all monitoring the Italy international, who is seeking regular first-team football after struggling for opportunities at Anfield.

stories.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: Where were today's drivers when F1 last raced at Sepang?
stories.summary: Formula 1 is heading to Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix; the south-east Asian nation providing an unusual setting for a race.
stories.body:
Formula 1 is heading to Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix; the south-east Asian nation providing an unusual setting for a race that should have taken place a) back in April and b) over 4,000 miles away.

The sport last raced at the Sepang International Circuit in 2017 -- meaning more than half of the grid are set to take it on for the first time. Some, meanwhile, weren't even teenagers on the day Max Verstappen triumphed ahead of Lewis Hamilton and Daniel Ricciardo.

Ahead of this weekend's race, ESPN has rounded up what all 22 drivers were doing at the time of that last Malaysian GP.

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

Lewis Hamilton
At the time, Hamilton was a three-time world champion, having won his first title with McLaren in 2008 before adding two more with Mercedes in 2014 and 2015. He would win a fourth in 2017 -- and returns to Malaysia nine years later with seven titles to his name.

During the race nine years ago he finished second to Verstappen, who was in his second season at Red Bull at the time.

Hamilton shares the record for most poles at Sepang with Michael Schumacher, with five each, and he was the last driver on the current grid to take pole here.

Charles Leclerc
The Monégasque was racing in Formula 2 with Prema Racing and was the runaway leader at the time.

Leclerc did, however, get a taste of an F1 weekend as -- not for the first time -- he competed in FP1 in place of Marcus Ericsson. He was three-tenths quicker than Pascal Wehrlein.

Leclerc went on to win the F2 drivers' championship that same year, earning himself a spot in the highest tier of motorsport a year later as a full-time F1 driver for Sauber.

Kimi Antonelli
The Mercedes driver, who is currently leading the drivers' championship and is on course to be the youngest to hold the title, has never raced in Malaysia. He was karting in Europe at the time and was only 11 years old.

Antonelli, now 20, is 66 points ahead of teammate George Russell and has eight career victories in what is only his second season in F1.

George Russell
In 2017, the Englishman was racing in GP3 with ART Grand Prix and went on to win the championship that year in his rookie season.

He later made his F1 debut for Williams in 2019, so missed out on racing in Malaysia by two years.

Fernando Alonso
Alonso, who is now the oldest driver on the grid at 45 years old, was racing for McLaren-Honda in 2017.

At the time he was driving an uncompetitive car and finished the season 15th in the title standings, scoring points in only five races.

In Malaysia, he finished outside the points in 11th.

Lance Stroll
The Canadian has been in F1 for longer than most on the grid and was racing for Williams at the time. He finished eighth and picked up four points in what was his rookie season.

Alex Albon
Albon was regularly racing against Leclerc in F2 for ART Grand Prix in 2017. He finished his rookie season in 10th and two years later he made his F1 debut for Toro Rosso.

After a stint at Red Bull and a year as its reserve driver, he then signed for Williams in 2022 and has been there for the last five seasons. He joins the majority of the grid in racing in Malaysia for the first time.

Carlos Sainz

The Spaniard is one of the drivers who has raced here before when he was driving for Toro Rosso.

But it didn't last for long as he only completed half the race after suffering a power unit issue, which forced him to retire from seventh place.

Lando Norris

Norris was another driver who was racing -- and winning a title -- in a junior series, clinching the European Formula 3 championship with Carlin.

During the same year he joined McLaren's Driver Development Programme, before making his F1 debut in 2019 with the team.

Oscar Piastri

The Australian was competing in the F4 British Championship and ended up finishing the season second. He was racing for TRS Arden Junior Racing Team.

Esteban Ocon
Ocon, soon to be an F1 free agent, was racing for Force India at the last race here in 2017 and finished with a point in 10th.

Oliver Bearman
The young Briton was still karting in the UK. In 2017, he won the Kartmasters British Grand Prix in the Honda Cadet category at the age of 12

Max Verstappen

F1's four-time world champion was competing in his first full season for Red Bull after getting promoted early into 2016 after just one year under his belt at Toro Rosso.

He was only 20 years old at the time of the last race in Malaysia, but he won from third place after a dominant drive.

Verstappen passed Hamilton on Lap 4 and he was in control of the race from there.

Isack Hadjar

Hadjar joins the list as one of the youngsters who has never raced here. He was 13 years old at the time and was karting in France before progressing to the international scene.

Liam Lawson
New Zealander Lawson was competing in Australia in the Formula 4 Championship and ended up finishing second with his team BRM at the age of 15.

Arvid Lindblad

In 2017, Arvid Lindblad was competing in British karting championships, specifically racing in the cadet categories IAME Cadet and Honda Cadet.

Lindblad is the youngest driver on the current grid and was only nine at the time of the last Malaysian GP.

Franco Colapinto

Colapinto was competing at a high level in karting and won the Argentine Pre-Junior Karting Championship the year before.

In 2017, he won the Buenos Aires Regional Championship in the junior class, before moving to the UK to continue his racing career.

Pierre Gasly

Gasly made his Formula 1 debut at the 2017 Malaysian Grand Prix, replacing Daniil Kvyat at Toro Rosso, and finished 14th.

Nico Hülkenberg

Hülkenberg was racing for Renault and finished down in 16th. The German driver had previously been at Force India.

Gabriel Bortoleto

Bortoleto was racing for CRG Factory Team in the OK Junior karting category in Europe after making the move from Brazil. He was 12 at the time.

He became a full-time F1 driver with Sauber in 2025, ahead of the team's transition to Audi.

Sergio Pérez

The Mexican driver has raced in Malaysia seven times during his F1 career. In 2017, he was racing for Force India and finished the race in sixth.

Valtteri Bottas

Bottas was Hamilton's Mercedes teammate and started fifth on the grid, finishing in the same position.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Girl fights for life after car hits group of NRL fans
stories.summary: A young girl remains in critical condition after a car ploughed into a crowd of NRL fans waving off the Newcastle Knights team bus ahead of the grand final.
stories.body:
A young girl remains in critical condition after a car ploughed into a crowd of NRL fans waving off the Newcastle Knights team bus ahead of the grand final.

Fans largely made up of families and children were lined up on Newcastle Link Road at the Transfield Drive roundabout about 9.30am on Saturday in NSW's Hunter region when the tragedy unfolded.

Police say a car hit multiple people in the crowd, with an 18-year-old P-plate driver arrested. He was taken to hospital for mandatory testing.

NSW Police said 10 people were injured and treated at the scene before being transported to John Hunter Hospital in Newcastle.

A five-year-old girl and a 67-year-old man were initially in a critical condition, while eight other people, including a second five-year-old girl and a two-year-old girl, were in stable condition.

The young girl remains critical, while the man is now in a serious but stable condition.

The hospital provided an update to AAP on Saturday night confirming five other patients are in a stable condition and three others have been discharged.

The 18-year-old driver is expected to soon be charged, police say.

Assistant Commissioner Dave Waddell said two other people in the car were escorted from the crash scene after the crowd turned on them.

Mr Waddell said police did not believe the incident was deliberate but declined to comment on reports the vehicle was being driven erratically before the accident.

"I'll let the investigators from the crash investigation unit deal with that," he told reporters.

NSW Ambulance spokesman Tim Troon thanked bystanders who assisted responders.

"We did get a lot of bystander support during this incident, and it made our job carrying out emergency service a lot easier as a result," he told reporters.

NSW Premier Chris Minns said it was heartbreaking to see fans waving their team off involved in a terrible accident.

"We've seen how this grand final has brought Newcastle together, and I hope the whole community remains united as we continue to respond," he said in a statement.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he had spoken to the premier and offered his support.

"My thoughts are with everyone injured or involved in the horrible incident this morning in Newcastle," he said.

Newcastle Knights chief executive Peter Parr expressed deep concern for those impacted.

"What was meant to be a special morning for our community, thousands of Novocastrians coming together to farewell our team and show their support ahead of the grand final, has understandably turned into a distressing morning," he said.

"Newcastle is a strong community. We have seen that strength throughout this week, and today we need to draw on it again with compassion, care and support for those who need it most."

Knights captain Kalyn Ponga shared his thoughts in an Instagram story, sending love and support to all affected on behalf of the team.

"We're thinking of you, your families and everyone in our Newcastle community," he wrote.

Australian Rugby League Commission executive chairman Peter V'landys said the commission was working with police to understand the circumstances behind the incident.

In a post on social media, federal member for Hunter Dan Repacholi cited reports of a car doing a burnout before losing control.

Newcastle Mayor Gavin Morris said the crash was particularly upsetting given the environment of positivity and support heading into the grand final.

"We've been able to come together in an extraordinary way, and I believe now we will come together again in a new way," he told ABC News.

A large crowd had lined Newcastle's streets on Saturday morning to farewell the Knights players after the elation of reaching Sunday's NRL decider against the Sydney Roosters prompted an avalanche of fan support.
